title: Gate quick tier: run every suite that reads a changed testdata file, and the kernel STEP suites when the importer changes

labels.name: source:agent
labels.description: Opened by an AI agent (not a human reporter)

labels.name: effort:medium
labels.description: One module or crate, a known pattern (issue-worker-medium)

labels.name: P5
labels.description: Agent surface and tooling keep up with what shipped

body:
**What happens:** the quick tier picks suites from the gate maps. PR #2664 (STEP importer + a new fixture `testdata/models/bar_cross_holes.step`) passed its quick gate and its review, then turned two suites red on main (#2713): `app feature_edge_g1_join` and `kernel step_agreement`. Neither is named by the gate map of `app::geometry::import`, and kernel suites run in quick only when kernel code changes. `cargo xtask gate quick --dry-run` on the fix PR #2728 shows the same gap (20 suites selected, not those two).

**Proposal (two rules in the quick plan):**
1. **Test data:** a diff that adds, removes or changes a file under `testdata/` (or a test fixture/golden dir) selects every suite whose source reads that directory (a plain text search of the test sources for the path).
2. **Importers:** a diff under the STEP/mesh import code (`crates/app/src/geometry/import/`, the solidcraft import) also selects the kernel STEP suites (`step_agreement`, `machining_mesh`) and `app feature_edge_g1_join`.

**Done means:** `cargo xtask gate quick --dry-run` on #2664's diff selects `feature_edge_g1_join` and `kernel step_agreement`; pinned by an xtask plan unit test.

Interim: mkinney's pool reviewers already run these two rules by hand (review prompt, 2026-11-19). The larger fixes are parallel test runs (#2727) and coverage-based selection (#2738).
